;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Insurgency in the Maghreb (2002–present)|Maghreb insurgency]]
**[[Canada|Canadian]] national [[2019 Burkina Faso government resignation#Kidnapping and murder of Canadian nationals|Édith Blais]] and her [[Italians|Italian]] partner Luca Tacchetto are found alive in [[Mali]] after escaping from their captors. The pair were abducted in [[Burkina Faso]] on December 15, 2018. [https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/montreal/edith-blais-found-1.5497963 (CBC)]
*[[2020 Camp Taji attacks|Camp Taji attacks]]
**A second rocket attack this week hits the [[Camp Taji]] base in [[Baghdad Governorate]], [[Iraq]], wounding three [[United States troops]]. [https://abcnews.go.com/Politics/us-troops-wounded-rocket-attack-iraq-base/story?id=69598177 (ABC News)]

;Business and economy
*[[Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[Apple Inc.]] says it will close all of its stores outside [[China]] for two weeks in response to the coronavirus [[pandemic]], according to its [[CEO]] [[Tim Cook]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/mar/14/apple-closes-all-stores-across-world-outside-china-due-to-covid-19 (''The Guardian'')]
**[[Solomon Islands]] bans all travelers from China, [[South Korea]] and [[Japan]]. Health minister [[Dickson Mua]] also says that the country has suspended flights to [[Brisbane]], [[Australia]], and banned all [[civil servant]]s from overseas travel in an effort to contain [[COVID-19]]. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/411723/covid-19-solomons-extends-restrictions (RNZ)]
**[[American Airlines]] says it will suspend long haul international flights from March 16 until May 6. [https://finance.yahoo.com/news/american-airlines-suspend-nearly-long-030100859.html (Yahoo! News)]
**[[Walmart]] says all of its stores will reduce their hours to 6:00 a.m. until 11:00 p.m. local time until further notice in response to the pandemic. Several other chains have already done so. [https://www.cnn.com/2020/03/14/business/walmart-store-hours/index.html (CNN)]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 vaccine]]
***A group of researchers in the [[Netherlands]] have found antibodies that can be used to combat COVID-19. [https://nltimes.nl/2020/03/14/dutch-researchers-first-find-covid-19-antibodies-report (''NL Times'')]
***Scientists from [[Imperial College London]] say that a [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]] could be tested soon. [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/health/coronavirus-vaccine-news-update-cases-clinical-testing-trials-a9402101.html (''The Independent'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Spain]]
****[[Travel during the COVID-19 pandemic]]
*****[[Jet2.com]] planes return to the [[United Kingdom]] after the airline cancelled flights to [[Balearic Islands]] and [[Canary Islands]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-51887707 (BBC News)]
****[[2020 Spain coronavirus lockdown]]
*****[[Spain]] officially places the entire country in a lockdown for two weeks after declaring a Status Alarm the day before. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/europe/coronavirus-spain-nationwide-lockdown/2020/03/14/3bec8690-6619-11ea-8a8e-5c5336b32760 (''Washington Post'')]
****[[Javier Solana]], former [[Secretary General of NATO]] and former [[High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy]], has been hospitalized since Wednesday after [[COVID-19 testing|testing]] positive for COVID-19. [https://www.usnews.com/news/top-news/articles/2020-03-13/former-nato-chief-javier-solana-has-coronavirus-source (US News)]
****[[Spain]]'s [[Ministry of Health (Spain)|Ministry of Health]] reports more than 1,500 new confirmed cases of [[COVID-19]] in a single day, including over a thousand in the capital [[Madrid]]. [https://www.euronews.com/2020/03/09/coronavirus-italy-becomes-most-affected-country-after-china (Euronews)]
****María Begoña Gómez Fernández, spouse of [[Prime Minister of Spain|Prime Minister]] [[Pedro Sánchez]], tests positive for coronavirus. [https://www.elconfidencial.com/espana/2020-03-14/la-mujer-de-pedro-sanchez-begona-gomez-da-positivo-en-coronavirus_2498712/ (''El Confidencial'')] [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-spain-gomez/spanish-pms-wife-has-tested-positive-for-coronavirus-pms-offfice-idUSKBN21117B (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
****A newborn baby tests positive for COVID-19 at [[North Middlesex University Hospital]] in [[Edmonton, London|Edmonton]], [[London]], becoming the youngest known victim of the disease in the [[United Kingdom]]. The child's mother has also tested positive for the disease. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/mar/14/newborn-baby-tests-positive-for-coronavirus-in-london (''The Guardian'')]
****[[NHS England]] reports 10 more deaths from the coronavirus, doubling the number of deaths in the UK to 21. All patients were aged over 70 and had underlying health conditions. [https://www.standard.co.uk/news/uk/uk-coronavirus-death-toll-hits-21-nhs-england-a4387426.html (''Daily Standard'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Italy]], [[2020 Italy coronavirus lockdown]]
****[[Italy]]'s [[Ministry of Health (Italy)|Ministry of Health]] reports 250 more deaths from COVID-19, the highest number of deaths in a single 24-hour period in the country to date. The Mayor of [[Bergamo]] [[Giorgio Gori]] says churches are now being used to store dead bodies as the city's morgues are full. [https://www.skynews.com.au/details/_6141612273001 (Sky News)] 
****Air pollution in [[Northern Italy]] drops following the coronavirus lockdown. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-italy-pollution-idUSKBN2102X4 (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in San Marino]]
****The Government of the [[Republic of San Marino]] orders a nationwide quarantine until April 6. [https://www.sanmarinortv.sm/news/politica-c2/nuovo-decreto-legge-in-vigore-fino-al-6-aprile-a185082 (San Marino RTV)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Africa]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Morocco]]
****[[Abdelkader Aamara]], [[Ministry of Equipment, Transport and Logistics (Morocco)|Minister of Equipment, Transport and Logistics]] and [[House of Representatives (Morocco)|Deputy]] tests positive for COVID-19. [https://www.straitstimes.com/world/africa/coronavirus-morocco-halts-flights-with-25-more-countriesv (''Straits Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Namibia]]
****[[Namibia]] reports its first two cases of [[COVID-19]]. [[President of Namibia|President]] [[Hage Geingob]] says he imposes a travel ban to and from [[Qatar]], [[Ethiopia]] and [[Germany]] for 30 days. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-namibia/namibia-reports-first-two-cases-of-coronavirus-imposes-travel-ban-idUSKBN2110CX?il=0 (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Rwanda]]
****[[Rwanda]] confirms the country's first case of coronavirus, an Indian citizen who arrived in the country on March 8 from [[Mumbai]]. [https://www.newtimes.co.rw/news/coronavirus-rwanda-confirms-first-case (''The New Times'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Iran]]
****[[Iran]] reports 1,365 new confirmed cases of [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]] and 97 more deaths, the highest number of deaths in a single 24-hour period in the country to date, bringing the total to 12,729 confirmed cases and 611 deaths. [https://gulfnews.com/world/mena/coronavirus-iran-reports-97-new-deaths-taking-total-to-611-1.1584183312687 (''Gulf News'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia]]
****[[Budi Karya Sumadi]], the [[Ministry of Transportation (Indonesia)|Indonesian Minister of Transportation]], tests positive for COVID-19. [https://www.antaranews.com/berita/1356658/menhub-budi-karya-sumadi-positif-covid-19 (Antara News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Syria]]
****[[Syria]]'s [[Government of Syria|government]] closes all schools and cancels public events until April 2, to prevent the spread of the virus. Syrian Minister Imad al-Azab rejects claims the government is covering up cases and says the new measures are "precautionary". [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-syria/syria-insisting-it-is-coronavirus-free-takes-broad-steps-to-prevent-spread-idUSKBN2110SA (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Donald Trump]] confirms he has been tested for COVID-19, after coming into contact with [[President of Brazil|Brazilian President]] [[Jair Bolsonaro]]'s Press Secretary last week, who has been diagnosed with the disease. President Trump's results were negative. [https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/politics/2020/03/14/coronavirus-trumps-white-house-doctor-says-he-doesnt-need-test/5049602002/ (''USA Today'')] [https://www.cnbc.com/2020/03/14/trump-tests-negative-for-coronavirus-white-house-doctor-says.html (CNBC)]
***A total of 16 [[U.S. state|U.S. states]] have closed all of their schools as of this date. [https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/health/2020/03/14/coronavirus-updates-trump-may-get-tested-house-passes-relief-bill/5032571002/ (''USA Today'')] 
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in New York (state)]]
****[[New York (state)|New York]] [[Governor of New York|Governor]] [[Andrew Cuomo]] reports his state has confirmed 613 cases of COVID-19, with two deaths today. [https://www.pix11.com/news/coronavirus/ny-state-now-has-613-positive-covid-19-cases-cuomo-says (WPIX)] [https://www.nbcnewyork.com/news/local/tri-state-braces-for-further-covid-19-spread-after-house-house-emergency-bill/2326406/ (WNBC)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in California]]
****[[Contra Costa County, California|Contra Costa County]] bans gatherings over 100 people, effective March 15. This is more than twice as strict as Governor [[Gavin Newsom]]'s ban of crowds of 250 or more people earlier in the week. [https://www.mercurynews.com/2020/03/14/coronavirus-contra-costa-county-bans-gatherings-of-100-or-more-for-march (''San Jose Mercury News'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Michigan]]
****[[Michigan]] reports eight more confirmed cases of COVID-19 since yesterday, for a total of 33. [https://www.clickondetroit.com/news/local/2020/03/15/michigan-announced-8-new-positive-covid-19-cases-33-cases-total/ (WDIV)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Georgia (U.S. state)]]
****After 66 cases of COVID-19 are confirmed in [[Georgia (U.S. state)|Georgia]], [[Governor of Georgia|Governor]] [[Brian Kemp]] declares a [[State of emergency#United States|public health emergency]]. [https://www.ajc.com/news/state--regional-govt--politics/kemp-declares-unprecedented-public-health-emergency-georgia/gdTeQfD6zJPb1kbYlRLHRO/ (''Atlanta Journal-Constitution'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Colorado]]
****In an unprecedented move, [[Colorado]] [[Governor of Colorado|Governor]] [[Jared Polis]] orders the closure of all downhill ski areas for a week, citing coronavirus concerns. [https://coloradosun.com/2020/03/14/jared-polis-executive-order-ski-resorts/ (''The Colorado Sun'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand]]
***[[New Zealand]] [[Prime Minister of New Zealand|Prime Minister]] [[Jacinda Ardern]] imposes a 14 day mandatory quarantine to everyone arriving in New Zealand, including diplomats, tourists and returning citizens, but excluding those coming in from Pacific Island nations, and bans all cruise ships from entering the nation until at least June 30. [https://www.news.com.au/lifestyle/health/health-problems/coronavirus-spanish-towns-in-lockdown-as-covid19-hurricane-sweeps-across-the-country/news-story/d3e56e2b7948fb08b3d54c8c74a5d596 (News.com.au)]
